title: How do I report a claim?
body: You can report a claim 24 hours a day by calling 1-800-555-0188, through your online account at portal.marlowecrest.example, or through your agent. Have your policy number and a description of what happened ready. Photos help but are not required to start a claim.

title: What happens after I report a claim?
body: We'll send you a letter or email confirming your claim number. An adjuster will be assigned to your claim and will contact you to discuss the damage and next steps. For some smaller claims we may be able to settle using your photos without an inspection.

title: Should I make repairs before the adjuster visits?
body: Make temporary repairs that stop more damage, like tarping a roof or shutting off water. Keep your receipts, because reasonable temporary repair costs are usually part of the claim. Please wait on permanent repairs until your adjuster has seen the damage or agreed that you can proceed.

title: Will filing a claim raise my premium?
body: Not necessarily. Your claims history is one of many factors we use when pricing your renewal. Small weather claims affecting many homes in the same area are treated differently from repeated claims at the same home.

title: What if I disagree with a claim decision?
body: Start by talking to your adjuster. Often a disagreement comes down to missing information, like a contractor estimate or photos. If you still disagree, your decision letter explains how to ask for a review by a claims team lead who was not involved in the original decision.

title: Why did my premium go up?
body: Premiums can change at renewal because of the cost to rebuild homes in your area, your home's claims history, changes to discounts, and rate changes approved for everyone with your policy type. Your agent can walk you through the specific reasons for your policy.

title: Will you tell me before my premium goes up?
body: Yes. If your premium is going up by more than 15% at renewal, we'll send you a letter at least 30 days before your renewal date explaining the change. Every customer also receives their renewal Declarations page and bill before the renewal date.

title: What payment options do you offer?
body: You can pay in full, in two installments, or monthly by automatic bank draft. Installment fees apply to two pay and monthly plans. You can pay online, by phone, by mail, or through your agent.

title: What happens if I miss a payment?
body: We'll send you a reminder. If the payment is still not received, we will mail a notice of cancellation that tells you the date your policy will end if we don't receive payment. Pay in full before that date and your coverage continues without a gap.

title: Why is my policy not being renewed?
body: Your nonrenewal notice gives the reason we made this decision. If you believe the information we used is out of date, for example your roof has been replaced, call your agent or our Underwriting Services team at 1-800-555-0172 as soon as possible.

title: How much notice will I get if my Kessington policy is not renewed?
body: For homes in Kessington, we mail a nonrenewal notice at least 30 days before your policy expires, and the notice states the reason.

title: How do I add someone who can talk to you about my policy?
body: You can add up to two authorized contacts by calling Customer Care or through your online account. An authorized contact can discuss your policy and claims with us and make payments for you. They cannot make changes to your coverage.

title: How is my dwelling coverage amount decided?
body: Your dwelling coverage (Coverage A) should reflect what it would cost to rebuild your home, not its market value. We use construction details about your home and local building costs to calculate a rebuild cost. Your agent can help you review this if you have made improvements.

title: Does homeowners insurance cover flooding?
body: No. Flood damage, including surface water and overflow of rivers, is excluded from Crestline and Cottage Basic policies. Flood insurance is available separately through the national flood program and private insurers. Ask your agent.

title: Does my policy cover sewer or drain backup?
body: Not automatically. You can add Water Back-Up coverage to a Crestline policy with limits of $5,000, $10,000, or $25,000. Cottage Basic does not offer this coverage.

title: What is the difference between Crestline and Cottage Basic?
body: Crestline is a broad homeowners policy that covers your home against all risks except those excluded, and includes theft, water damage, and liability. Cottage Basic is a lower cost policy for smaller or seasonal homes that covers named causes of loss like fire and wind. It does not cover theft or water damage.

title: Can I go paperless?
body: Yes. Sign in to your online account and choose Documents > Delivery Preferences, or call Customer Care. You'll receive an email when new documents are available. You can switch back to paper at any time.

title: Do you offer a discount for water leak sensors?
body: Yes. Crestline customers in Norvale who install a qualifying monitored water leak detection device can receive a discount. Send a photo of the installed device or the monitoring invoice to your agent.

title: What is a named storm deductible?
body: In certain coastal counties in Kessington, a separate deductible applies to damage from a named storm. It is shown as a percentage of your dwelling coverage on your Declarations page.

title: How do I update my mortgage company?
body: Send us the new mortgage company name, address, and loan number through your online account or by asking your agent. We'll send updated evidence of insurance to the new lender.

title: Can I cancel my policy in the middle of the term?
body: Yes. Contact your agent or Customer Care. Any unearned premium is refunded to your original payment method or by check within 15 business days.

title: Is Crestline Select still available?
body: Crestline Select is no longer sold. All Crestline Select customers were moved to the Crestline Homeowners Policy at renewal by 2024.

title: Do you insure apartment buildings?
body: Marlowe Crest Commercial Lines offers a Landlord Package for apartment buildings of 5 to 40 units in Norvale. Please contact a Marlowe Crest commercial agent.

title: What do I do if my home is not livable after a loss?
body: Call us right away. If your policy includes loss of use coverage, we can help with hotel or rental costs while your home is repaired. In many cases we can issue an advance the same day.
